title: Lean Thinking: A Strategy for Operational Excellence
overview: Lean Thinking is a transformative approach aimed at achieving operational excellence within organizations. If your organization’s strategy includes operational and organizational excellence, this course will provide valuable insights and practical tools. Participants will learn how to develop a Lean strategy, define objectives, and explore a wide range of Lean tools. The course also provides guidance on initiating and sustaining a Lean journey within their organizations.
audience: This course is ideal for professionals involved in operational excellence initiatives, process improvement, and performance optimization. It is especially beneficial for those responsible for measuring, linking, and improving organizational performance.
methodology: The course incorporates a mix of interactive exercises, ranging from simple to complex Lean applications. Participants will engage with tools such as Value Stream Mapping (VSM) and the 5S methodology, as well as analyze real-world case studies. Lectures, group discussions, and presentations will support the learning process and help participants achieve the course objectives.
competencies: Integration of Lean and Six Sigma
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Understand Lean concepts and their importance to organizations.
Identify common process waste and recognize its impact on profitability, competitive advantage, and customer satisfaction.
Learn how Lean principles can help reduce operating costs, cycle times, and non-value-added activities.
Develop a strategic and actionable Lean implementation plan.

items.text: Core concepts and the benefits of Lean
Identifying and eliminating the 8 types of waste
Implementing the 5S program (Sort, Straighten, Sweep, Systematize, Sustain)

Creating Spaghetti Diagrams for process visualization
